name: BULGARIA
lead: Bulgaria is in the Balkans. Old tombs hide under its wheat fields. Every May, valleys bloom pink to make the world's finest rose oil. Its name has barely changed since AD 681. It has snowy mountains, the Danube River, and a Black Sea coast, in a country about the size of Iceland.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: The Balkan Mountains cut across the middle. The Rhodope range rises in the south to Musala, the Balkans' highest peak. Between them lies the Thracian Plain, Europe's finest rose-growing valley.
The Danube forms the northern border. The Black Sea coast stretches 378 km in the east. Forests cover a third of the country, hiding lynx and brown bears.
animals: About 700 brown bears live in the Rhodope and Balkan mountains. The Dalmatian pelican nests on Srebarna Lake, a UNESCO wetland near the Danube.
Bulgaria's honeybees make some of Europe's best wildflower honey. The Karakachan shepherd dog has guarded flocks here for over 2,000 years.
culture: Every May, pickers harvest pink damask roses near Kazanlak before sunrise. Three tonnes of petals make one kilogram of rose oil for top perfumes.
Bulgarian folk music uses tricky rhythms like 7/8 or 11/16. In the horo chain dance, hundreds of people can link up in one huge circle.
history: Bulgaria began in AD 681, when Khan Asparuh joined Bulgar warriors with Slavic tribes. In the 9th century, pupils of Saints Cyril and Methodius created the Cyrillic alphabet.
Ottoman rule lasted nearly 500 years. Russia helped win independence in 1878. Communism ended in 1989 after peaceful protests. Bulgaria joined NATO in 2004 and the EU in 2007.
wows: Bulgaria gave the world Cyrillic, now used by over 250 million people.
The Rose Valley makes about 70% of the world's rose oil.
Musala is the tallest peak between the Alps and the Caucasus.
In Bulgaria, a nod means NO and a head shake means YES.
People have lived in Plovdiv for over 6,000 years.
UNESCO lists Kazanlak's Thracian tomb, with 2,300-year-old murals.
Yoghurt bacteria Lactobacillus bulgaricus was first found in Bulgarian yoghurt in 1905.

myths.myth: The oldest gold jewellery is Egyptian
myths.fact: Gold from graves near Varna, Bulgaria, is about 6,500 years old. Experts call it the oldest worked gold.
It is blue-green, like most seas. Experts still argue about its name.
